      type: object
      properties:

          title: Title

          example: DR

          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility as a flat address line; when structured address fields are
            supplied ('addressLine1'), they are preferred. On a response this carries the
            composed address (the normalized addressLine1, with a single space and the
            normalized addressLine2 appended when addressLine2 is present).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of the owner's structured postal address. Optional;
            when supplied (non-blank) the structured fields are preferred over the flat
            'address' input. Normalized like the flat address (trimmed, inner whitespace
            collapsed, upper-cased, common street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '10 King Street'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the owner's structured postal address
            (e.g. unit or apartment). Normalized like addressLine1 and, when present,
            appended to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The owner's postcode. Optional; when present it must be a 4-digit value
            and, when the city has a known region (Sydney -> NSW, Melbourne -> VIC,
            Brisbane -> QLD), must fall within that region's inclusive range (NSW 2000-2099,
            VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit
            postcode. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized
            to E.164 form; a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits.

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20

          title: Email address

## Summary

I converted owner deletion into a soft-delete across the Spring Boot stack:

**Domain model** — `Owner.java`
- Added a `deleted` boolean field (`@Column(name = "deleted", nullable = false)`) defaulting to `false`, with `isDeleted()`/`setDeleted()`. A newly created owner is therefore `deleted = false`.

**API contract** — `openapi.yml`
- Added a `deleted` boolean property to the `Owner` response schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps `owner.deleted → dto.deleted`. `GET /api/owners/{id}` now returns the flag.

**Controller** — `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`
- `deleteOwner` no longer removes the row; it sets `deleted = true` and saves, returning `204 NO_CONTENT` (2xx). The record is retained, and `GET` still returns it with `deleted: true`.
- The create endpoint's checks now ignore soft-deleted owners: filtered `existing.isDeleted()` out of `isDuplicate` (the identity-key gate), `findHousemates` (the household duplicate block), and `findPossibleDuplicateOf` (the possible-duplicate flag). So a normally-blocking duplicate is allowed when the only match is deleted.

**Persistence schema/seed** — added a `deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` column to all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres) and appended the value to the positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)` seed rows (hsqldb — used by the tests — and mysql; h2/postgres use named-column inserts that pick up the default).

Both new acceptance tests pass: `coreSoftDeleteFlagsAndRetains` (delete flags `deleted` true and retains the record) and `coreDeletedOwnerIgnoredByDuplicateCheck` (recreating a soft-deleted owner is allowed).

One note: the pre-existing MySQL seed data was already positionally inconsistent with the MySQL schema (8 insert values vs. many columns); I kept my change internally consistent by adding the matching value, but MySQL isn't exercised by the test suite (which runs on hsqldb).
